Q1: How much of the migration should this single issue/PR deliver?
Choices:
A) Everything in one PR: the bash helper and Python twin plus all 8 migration steps (hot paths, removing the inline retry copies, the sweep loop, the ~14 poller fallbacks, the Python readers, and the rate-limit-aware re-run of validation/review).
B) The shared bash helper and Python twin plus the hot-path steps 1–4 and 6 (the `> file`/`$()` sites, the `review_autofix.yml` gate, the `validate.yml` authorize step, the `implement.yml`/`orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` resolve calls, and the sweep loop). Steps 5, 7 and 8, and the "retry after reset instead of escalating" behaviour, are filed as follow-up issues that link back here. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Only the helper, its Python twin and the tests. Every call-site migration becomes a follow-up issue.
Q2: How should the "retry mutations only with `--idempotent`" rule apply to the existing `gh_retry`, `gh_retry_to_file` and `gh_api_json_to_file` callers (~68 POST creates go through them today)?
Choices:
A) Change the existing helpers. A POST (an explicit `-X`/`--method POST`, or `gh api` with `-f`/`-F`/`--input` and no explicit GET) makes one attempt unless the caller passes `--idempotent`. PUT, PATCH and DELETE stay retryable. In the same PR, add `--idempotent` to existing POST callers that are safe to repeat (label adds, `workflow_dispatch` guarded by a dedupe marker, and similar). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Leave the existing helpers' retry behaviour unchanged. Only the new shared helper enforces `--idempotent`, and callers adopt it as they migrate.
C) Change the existing helpers to refuse retries for every mutating method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) unless `--idempotent` is passed.
